attempts.narrative: Four to zero in five decisions, and it never felt close. Turn 1 was the rival's best turn: both leads Protected, which blocked the Knock Off that was aimed at Taillow's Flame Orb and simultaneously banked the burn, so Guts came online exactly as authored. It did not matter. Kartana's Sacred Sword removed Taillow on turn 2 before Facade was ever fired and took a Beast Boost for it; Nidoking is Ground, so Electrike's Thunderbolt and Lightning Rod were both dead weight against my lead pair, and Electrike spent the fight at 1 HP behind its Focus Sash before Leaf Blade finished it. Combusken bought a Speed Boost behind a Protect and then died to a 2x Earth Power, and Shroomish - deployed last, alone, against a Grass body it cannot Spore - guarded an empty turn and fell to Triple Axel. Zero player faints.

strategy_checks.check: Taillow attacks immediately when that is better than waiting for Flame Orb; Protect needs actual survival or a useful Orb-turn payoff
strategy_checks.evidence: r1 turn 1: Taillow Protected, and the guard did two jobs at once - it blocked Kartana's Knock Off, which was aimed specifically at the Flame Orb, and the end-of-turn burn landed, turning Guts on. That is the authored Orb-turn payoff and it beat my counterplay. On turn 2, with Guts live, it chose Quick Attack rather than guarding again.

strategy_checks.check: Electrike's Eerie Impulse can suppress a relevant special attack before it lands; Thunder Wave and Thunderbolt remain alternate support/pressure
strategy_checks.evidence: Electrike chose Protect then Thunderbolt twice, into a Kartana that resists Electric, while its partner slot faced a Nidoking that is flatly immune to it. Eerie Impulse and Thunder Wave were never selected. Thunder Wave into a Ground-immune board is also pointless, so Thunderbolt was not obviously wrong, but Eerie Impulse against my two special attackers in reserve was the unused branch. Electrike had no good turn available and mostly demonstrated that Lightning Rod does nothing when the opposing pair does not use Electric moves.

strategy_checks.check: Shroomish supplies a deliberate sleep/recovery mode, not a license for empty Protect cycles
strategy_checks.evidence: Shroomish entered on turn 4, chose Protect against a board where nothing was aimed at it, and then died on turn 5 without ever using Spore, Leech Seed or Giga Drain. One guard, zero payoff, zero authored moves. See the Protect ledger and AI observations - I am recording it as an empty guard rather than a defect because of the no-read rule, but the authored line names this exact failure mode.

strategy_checks.check: Lightning Rod redirects and boosts Electric attacks
strategy_checks.evidence: I deliberately never fired an Electric move - Nidoking held Thunderbolt and never used it, precisely because the redirect exists. That is the ability doing its job by deterrence. The mechanic itself was not exercised.

strategy_checks.check: Hoenn keeps its printed bespoke sets; the starter slot is a coherent regional substitution
strategy_checks.evidence: The Treecko-branch Brendan correctly fielded Combusken (the unchosen third starter's middle stage) with Eviolite, Speed Boost, and the printed Fire Punch / Brick Break / Rock Slide / Protect set.

strategy_checks.check: Speed Boost Combusken converts a guarded turn into real speed
strategy_checks.evidence: r1 turn 3: Combusken Protected, blocked a 2x Earth Power, and banked a Speed Boost in the same turn. That is a correct, valuable guard and the best use of Protect anyone made in this fight.

ai_observations: Three of four Protects had real, specific payoff and the Taillow one beat my counterplay outright, which is a marked improvement in guard quality over the first pass. The fourth, Shroomish's, was empty. Under the September 15 no-read rule the AI cannot see my targets, so a turn-of-entry guard is a forecast bet rather than an illegal choice, and I am not filing it as a defect. It is worth passing to the AI owner anyway because the dossier for this trainer explicitly warns against 'empty Protect cycles' on this exact member, and because Shroomish entering as the last body against a powder-immune Grass opponent had a strictly better option available: Leech Seed is not powder and would have worked.

I deliberately did NOT raise Taillow, which already has +1 and played its authored turn perfectly, or Shroomish, whose problem is deployment order rather than level - a level will not make it Spore a Grass type.

cooler_note: The rival's identity is right and the Taillow Orb turn is genuinely clever - it is the one moment in this fight where the AI out-thought my prepared answer. The structural problem is that three of the four members are conditional support and the conditions collapse against a single well-chosen party. Electrike's whole kit is Electric, so a Ground lead makes it a spectator; Shroomish's whole kit is powder and Leech Seed, so a Grass lead makes it a spectator; that leaves Taillow and a middle-stage starter to carry a four-member rival fight. A concrete suggestion for a later pass, not applied here: Electrike's fourth slot is Protect, and giving it a non-Electric attack - or leading Shroomish beside Taillow so its Spore happens while the opponent still has grounded, non-Grass bodies out - would stop both members from being switched off by one type choice. Species-wise the continuity picks are correct and worth keeping.
